problem-clarity.title: Problem Clarity Fundamentals
problem-clarity.description: Learn how to clearly define and articulate the problem you're solving.
content: Welcome to Problem Clarity Fundamentals! In this lesson, you'll learn the essential skills for defining and articulating the problem your startup aims to solve.

## Why Problem Clarity Matters

Many startups fail not because they can't build a solution, but because they never truly understood the problem they were solving. Clear problem definition is the foundation of a successful venture.

## The Problem Statement Framework

1. **Who** has the problem?
2. **What** is the specific pain point?
3. **When** does this problem occur?
4. **Why** is this problem important to solve?
5. **How** are people currently dealing with it?

## Key Takeaways

• A well-defined problem is half-solved
• Talk to your target users regularly
• Be specific - avoid vague problem statements
• Validate that the problem is worth solving
• Document everything you learn

## Next Steps

Take 30 minutes to write down your problem statement using the framework above. Share it with 3 potential customers and get their feedback.

target-market.title: Understanding Your Target Market
target-market.description: Discover how to identify and deeply understand your ideal customers.
content: Welcome to Understanding Your Target Market! This lesson will help you identify and deeply understand your ideal customers.

## The Importance of Market Understanding

Knowing your target market isn't just about demographics - it's about understanding their behaviors, motivations, and pain points deeply.

## Building Your Ideal Customer Profile

1. **Demographics**: Age, location, income, education
2. **Psychographics**: Values, interests, lifestyle
3. **Behaviors**: How they currently solve problems
4. **Pain Points**: What keeps them up at night
5. **Goals**: What they're trying to achieve

## Market Research Methods

• Customer interviews (minimum 20-30)
• Surveys and questionnaires
• Social media listening
• Competitor analysis
• Industry reports and data

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

• Assuming everyone is your customer
• Relying solely on assumptions
• Not talking to real potential customers
• Ignoring negative feedback
• Not updating your understanding over time

## Action Items

Create a detailed profile of your ideal customer. Then, find and interview 5 people who match this profile. Document what you learn.
